We propose a study that uses financial regulator as a bridge: first, review how flash crash and optimal trading are each currently treated through financial regulator; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.

Both are already linked to 114 common concepts, including sum game, centralized exchange and liquidity shock, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses sum game as a bridge: first, review how electronic market and trading cost are each currently treated through sum game; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
quant-1343-4874.phd: A 3-4 year programme building a unified framework for electronic market and trading cost. Year 1: systematic review of the 114 shared concepts (starting with sum game, centralized exchange and liquidity shock); years 2-3: develop and validate a joint method; year 4: generalise it and release open tools and data.
quant-1343-4874.masters: A 6-12 month project: reproduce one recent electronic market study and one recent trading cost study, then run a focused experiment combining the two through sum game, reporting what transfers and what does not.
quant-1343-4874.industry: Illustrative example only (no claim about the firm's actual work): an industry research team such as Marshall Wace could run a short feasibility study testing whether combining electronic market with trading cost via sum game adds measurable value to an existing quant pipeline, then decide whether to invest further.
